**Logician**  
How To Play

Logician is an amalgam of logic (in a very pure, mathematical, set theory sense) and the arcane via the tarot and some elements of random chance.  Logician is played on a board with 10 hexes.  Your goal is to build different structures on the board and to then elevate them into larger, more powerful versions.  Each hex can have exactly one of each type of structure (pools, pyramids, towers, and fortresses) built on it.  Pools are represented by 2-sided "coins", pyramids are represented by 4-sided dice, towers are represented by 6-sided dice, and fortresses are represented by a hexagonal wall around the other structures. The three basic structures can be built at will, but a fortress can only be built on a hex where you already have one of each of the three basic structures.  The hexes on the board are broken up into four different terrain types Prairies, Forests, Mountains, and Swamps corresponding to the four tarot suits Swords, Wands, Cups, and Pentacles respectively.   
![][image1]  
*fig. 1—game board*

**Setup:** First, each player builds one of each of the three basic structures (a pool, a pyramid, and a tower) into hexes that do not currently have one of those structures in them.  Each player then draws three Logic cards and three Effect cards from the stacks.  Three tarot cards are then turned face up along the board.  Each of the Minor Arcana tarot cards (roughly corresponding to a standard deck of playing cards) has a defined set of targets (or operands in the math/logic vernacular; see fig. 2 below) corresponding to the card's suit/terrain-type and a structure level for values one to six.  Cards valued seven to ten correspond to the four structure types.  The Major Arcana tarot cards (Death, The Devil, The Fool, The Emperor, etc) have bigger/fancier effects that are detailed for each one and have some sort of tie-in to the card's character.

**Turn, Phase 1:** On the start of a turn, you can build one new structure (pool, pyramid, or tower) into a hex that does not yet have one of that type of structure on it.  The new structures enter play at their lowest level, so you make sure that numbered face is up on the piece.  Pools enter play at level two and have a maximum level of three.  Pyramids enter play at level one and have a maximum level of four.  Towers enter play at level one and have a maximum level of six.  Fortresses enter play at level one and have a maximum level of two.  If a hex already has a pool, pyramid, and tower belonging to you, you can optionally build a fortress around those three structures.   If you play a fortress on your turn, that ends your turn and you do not take the next phase.

**Turn, Phase 2:** During the second phase of your turn, you may do one of two things.  The first, and most common option, is to cast a logic spell.  To cast a logic spell you select one of your Logic Cards, and one of your Effect Cards and play it into one of the three Tarot cards.  The two items that the minor-arcana Tarot Cards correspond to are substituted into the logical expression and the Effect Card’s effect is applied to those structures that meet the logical criteria.

Apart from casting a logic spell, you can alternately take a special action if there are one or more major-arcana Tarot Card that are face up.  Each of the major-arcana Tarot Cards has different special effects (see fig. 3 below).  Some are played immediately and others can be held for later use.

Once a spell has been cast, the effects should be applied to the affected structures and the newly attained level should be made the top value on the structure.  The Logic, Effect, and Tarot Cards involved should then be placed in the respective discard piles.

If a structure’s level is downgraded below zero it is destroyed and returned to the player’s supply of structures and can be played again later.  Pools (which can only be level two or three) can only be destroyed by a "Downgrade 2" or more powerful effect (pushing its effective level to zero).

Once a fortress is played, the structures within are protected from effects, so they can't be downgraded until the fortress itself is destroyed.  This gives you a measure of protection from your opponent’s spells, but it also means your upgrade spells will not affect those structures inside a fortress either, so deciding when to play a fortress is important.

The goal of the game is to reach 40 victory points.  Your victory points are the sum total of all of your structures' levels.

**Minor-Arcana Operands**

|  Value | (Wands) Forests | (Cups) Mountains | (Swords) Prairies | (Pentacles) Swamps |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Ace | Forests / Lvl. 1 | Mountains / Lvl. 1 | Prairies / Lvl. 1 | Swamps / Lvl. 1 |
| 2 | Forests / Lvl. 2 | Mountains / Lvl. 2 | Prairies / Lvl. 2 | Swamps / Lvl. 2 |
| 3 | Forests / Lvl. 3 | Mountains / Lvl. 3 | Prairies / Lvl. 3 | Swamps / Lvl. 3 |
| 4 | Forests / Lvl. 4 | Mountains / Lvl. 4 | Prairies / Lvl. 4 | Swamps / Lvl. 4 |
| 5 | Forests / Lvl. 5 | Mountains / Lvl. 5 | Prairies / Lvl. 5 | Swamps / Lvl. 5 |
| 6 | Forests / Lvl. 6 | Mountains / Lvl. 6 | Prairies / Lvl. 6 | Swamps / Lvl. 6 |
| 7 | Forests / Pool | Mountains / Pool | Prairies / Pool | Swamps / Pool |
| 8 | Forests / Pyramid | Mountains / Pyramid | Prairies / Pyramid | Swamps / Pyramid |
| 9 | Forests / Tower | Mountains / Tower | Prairies / Tower | Swamps / Tower |
| 10 | Forests / Fortress | Mountains / Fortress | Prairies / Fortress | Swamps / Fortress |
| Page | Pyramid / Lvl. 1 | Pool / Lvl. 1 | Fortress / Lvl. 1 | Tower / Lvl. 1 |
| Knight | Pyramid / Lvl. 2 | Pool / Lvl. 2 | Fortress / Lvl. 2 | Tower / Lvl. 2 |
| Queen | Pyramid / Lvl. 3 | Pool / Lvl. 3 | Tower / Lvl. 3 | Tower / Lvl. 3 |
| King | Pyramid / Lvl. 4 | Pool / Lvl. 4 | Tower / Lvl. 4 | Tower / Lvl. 4 |

*fig. 2—Minor-Arcana Operands*

**Major-Arcana Actions**

**The Fool** \- Take this card from the active tarot area and save it on the table in front of you.  You may play this card at any time. If played during opponent's turn, this card can be used after that player has committed to a tarot/logic/effect play, but before the effects of that tarot are executed.  The effect switches the 'A' and 'B' operands for that pending spell.  
	  
**Strength** \- Downgrade one of your own structures by 1. Every unfortified structure of that same type controlled by your opponent is also downgraded by 1.  
	  
**The High Priestess** \- Take this tarot from the active area and place it on the table in front of you. You may play this card at any time you choose, though it must be played at the beginning of your turn, in conjunction with placing a structure. The chosen structure enters play at VP level 3, (unless it is a fortification, in which case it enters play at level 2\)  
	  
**The Empress** \- Take this card from the active tarot area and save it on the table in front of you. You may play this card at any time. If played during opponent's turn, this card can be used after that player has committed to a tarot/logic/effect, but before the effects of that tarot are executed. Choose a terrain type. Until the end of the current turn, all tiles of the chosen terrain type temporarily transform into a second terrain type of your choice. Afterward, resume play as usual, using the new terrain type for any calculations.  
	  
**The Emperor** \- Take this card from the active tarot area and save it on the table in front of you. You may play this card at any time. If played during opponent's turn, this card can be used after that player has committed to a tarot/logic/effect play, but before the effects of that tarot are executed. The current tarot in play is negated--discard it without calculating any effects.  
	  
**The Hierophant** \- Take this card from the active tarot area and save it on the table in front of you. You may play this card during any player's turn, but it must be played in response to a "randomize" effect. Choose any one target structure that would be randomized. That target is no longer randomized. Instead, upgrade or downgrade that structure to the level of your choice. Normal rules and effects of randomization apply to all other, non-target structures.  
	  
**The Lovers**  \- Choose a VP level. The opponent sitting clockwise from you chooses a terrain type. Using the chosen criteria, play this card as a normal tarot, using logic and effect from your hand as per the standard rules.  
	  
**MAGICIAN-** Look at opponent’s hand exchange one logic and effect of your choice with them

**The Chariot**  \- Choose one unfortified hex. Redistribute the levels of all structures on that hex among themselves however you like — the total is conserved, and no structure is destroyed or created.  
	  
**The Hermit** 	After this card has been played, discard all of the currently tarot cards from the active area. You may search through the deck and choose any three tarot cards to replace them as the active tarots for the next turn.  
	  
**Wheel of Fortune**  \- Choose any three target structures. Randomize.  
	  
**Justice**  \- Choose a terrain type. The opponent sitting clockwise from you chooses a VP level. Using the chosen criteria, play this card as a normal tarot, using logic and effect from your hand as per the standard rules.  
	  
**The Hanged Man** \- Choose a terrain type. The opponent sitting counter-clockwise from you chooses a structure type. Using the chosen criteria, play this card as a normal tarot, using logic and effect from your hand as per the standard rules.  
	  
**Death** \- Destroy all structures with VP level 2 or below, including those protected by fortifications.   
	  
**Temperance** \- Calculate all players' current VP, and determine which player's VP is lowest. All other players must downgrade or destroy their own structures until all players in the game have equal VP. Players can downgrade their structures in any way they choose.  
	  
**The Devil**  \- The opponent sitting clockwise from you must name a terrain type, structure type, or level. The next clockwise opponent must name a second condition different than the first. Using these named conditions, play this tarot card as normal, using a logic card from your hand, but no effect card. The effect for The Devil is always destroy.  
	  
**The Tower**  \- Target any one of your own structures, noting its VP level as VP=X. Then target one or more of opponents' structures, with total VP of these targets equal to X. Destroy all targeted structures, including your own.  
	  
**The Star**  \- Calculate all players' current VP, and determine which player's VP is greatest. All other players may choose to upgrade their own structures or place new structures until all players in the game have equal VP. Players can upgrade their structures in any way they choose (following legal placement rules).  
	  
**The Moon**  \- Choose a structure type. The opponent sitting counter-clockwise from you chooses a terrain type. Using the chosen criteria, play this card as a normal tarot, using logic and effect from your hand as per the standard rules.  
	  
**The Sun**  \- Choose a VP level. The opponent sitting counter-clockwise from you chooses a structure type. Using the chosen criteria, play this card as a normal tarot, using logic and effect from your hand as per the standard rules.  
	  
**Judgement** \- Minimize all structures on the board, including structures inside fortifications. The fortifications themselves remain in place. 

**The World** \- Play this tarot without playing any logic or effects cards. Instead, name a terrain, level, or type of structure. Name a second condition, different than the first. Name your chosen logic. Using your named conditions and logic, determine the targeted structures of this tarot as normal.  The effect of this tarot is Upgrade 1\.  
*fig. 3—Major-Arcana Actions*
